answer: Behavioural fingerprint persistence scoring. Each identity carries a compact sketch of its action history (timing, call graphs, value flows) that is compared against its next-epoch behaviour; a low match triggers a marble-like hardness penalty, decaying trust and throttling the identity's market access. Because a sybil cluster must keep every clone consistent across epochs, an attacker pays continuous coordination and replay cost per clone, plus a ripple of failed matches that compounds with scale.
